title: Construction of downfolded Hamiltonians from projective transcorrelation
abstract: Projective transcorrelation recovers the short-range electron correlation by a similarity transformation with a geminal function $f(r_{12})$, at the cost of an effective Hamiltonian containing a 3-body term. We replace the term by an effective operator of rank at most two, obtained from the two-body cumulant (2C) approximation to the three-particle reduced density matrix. The 2C 3-body energy is written without cumulants, and the effective one- and two-body interactions are derived as its partial derivatives with respect to the reduced density matrices. The truncation is assessed on the atomization and reaction energies of the HEAT set with CCSD(T), and on the CAS-pTC model, whose downfolded Hamiltonian is held on a qubit register with the number of Pauli strings reduced from the sixth power of the orbital count to the fourth.
summary: This paper develops a method to simplify complex, high-order electron correlation Hamiltonians derived from projective transcorrelation (pTC). By employing the two-body cumulant (2C) approximation, the computationally prohibitive three-body terms are reduced to effective one- and two-body operators. This significantly lowers the computational scaling while maintaining high accuracy for molecular energy calculations.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the computational cost associated with high-order, three-body electron correlation terms arising from similarity transformations like projective transcorrelation (pTC).
main_result: The authors successfully approximate the problematic 3-body term using the two-body cumulant (2C) approximation, effectively reducing the required operator rank from potentially $M^6$ to two-body terms.
method: The method involves deriving effective one- and two-body interactions by taking partial derivatives of the approximated 3-body energy with respect to lower-order reduced density matrices.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to electronic structure calculations, specifically using the pTC method on molecular systems (e.g., N2) and assessed on the HEAT set for benchmarking.
key_observables: Atomization and reaction energies, dissociation energy of N2, and the reduction in Pauli string count on a qubit register.
important_parameters: The approximation relies on the 2C cumulant expansion, which discards connected three-particle correlation.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the 2C approximation to the three-particle reduced density matrix is sufficiently accurate to allow the effective Hamiltonian to be written in terms of one- and two-body operators.
figures_summary: The notes mention comparisons of calculated energies (e.g., N2 dissociation energy) against experimental values, showing the small error introduced by the 2C approximation.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the pTC Hamiltonian, details the necessity of approximating the 3-body term, derives the 2C approximation for this term, and concludes by benchmarking the resulting effective Hamiltonian on chemical accuracy benchmarks.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, mathematically rigorous pathway to tame high-order correlation effects in electronic structure theory, making previously intractable calculations feasible for larger systems or quantum simulation.

All methods are all-electron in the same basis and geometry. Species are ordered by size and the H atom is omitted, having no pTC step. Open squares are pTC with ∆HF alone, filled squares add ∆GBC.

FIG. 4. Mean absolute error of the atomization energies (up- per) and reaction energies (lower) against the HEAT refer- ence, as the one-particle basis is enlarged. The three bases left of the rule are frozen core and the two on its right all electron, so the abscissa is not a single basis-set series. HF, MP2 and CCSD(T) are the companion calculations without pTC for the frozen-core sets, and the values of Fig. 3 for the all-electron ones. ∆HF and ∆GBC are as in Fig. 3.

FIG. 5. Error of the atomization energies (upper) and re- action energies (lower) in the full-valence CAS space alone, against the HEAT reference. CASSCF/aug-cc-pVTZ orbitals, 1s frozen.
